title: Built an AI options trading agent (Claude Haiku + Sonnet) — first profitable day on paper: +Rs 3,141 on a gap-down reversal
author: Chennai_data_guy

comments.author: CryptographerBig7624
comments.body:
nice, the maker/checker split with fail-closed on error is a solid pattern, that alone puts you ahead of most single-prompt setups.

one gentle thing since you're clearly building this properly: one profitable paper day is basically noise, the error bars swamp a single session. the stuff that'll actually tell you if it works is the discipline you already showed today, the checker capping the against-trend lot and the three skips. that's the part worth measuring over a big sample. track your skips like real trades too, log what they would've done, otherwise you can't tell if the filter has edge or just reduces activity.

the "no historical indicator pollution" call is interesting, curious if that holds up out of sample or if it just fit today's gap-reversal nicely. that's the thing i'd stress test before trusting it.

genuinely good work though, the risk plumbing is the hard part and yours looks thought through

replies.author: Chennai_data_guy
replies.body:
Thanks! You nailed the two biggest challenges:

**Backtesting** — yeah, it's basically impossible with LLM-in-the-loop. Claude isn't deterministic, so you can't replay historical decisions. Our approach: we log every Claude input/output pair as training data. Once we have 500+ trades, we'll train a small deterministic model that mimics Claude's decision patterns but is reproducible and backtestable. The LLM is the teacher, the custom model is the student.

**API costs** — real concern. We just optimized this today actually — prompt caching cuts \~71% off the system prompt cost per cycle. We also track every API call with token counts and cost in a CSV, so we know exactly what we're spending. Currently \~$0.10/day for 5 cycles, aiming to get that lower.

Would love to see your data when you're ready to share. Comparing signals across different setups is probably the fastest way to figure out what's actually edge vs noise. Are you also on Indian markets or different?

comments.author: Headjacked
comments.body: HCTrading is an autonomous, deterministic trading system  built layer by layer — currently Layer 1, a multi-signal scanner (EMA/Donchian/RSI) that scores setups 0–100 and only acts above 70, with a fixed-fractional sizer (1% risk per trade, 2×ATR stops, $500 cap, 25% equity cap) and a fail-closed checker that independently re-verifies every trade before it can fire. It runs on a DigitalOcean droplet (FastAPI backend, Cloudflare Worker dashboard) against Alpaca for US equities, with execution currently hardcoded off while we build and test
